source.note: The mirror passed the independently frozen DATESTAMP gate; the GIS result is therefore interpreted as a spatial-feasibility audit, not as a source-delivery failure.

interpretation: The strict 2024 map-based bare-control gate fails because Lower Tampa Bay contributes only one mapped-edge candidate despite 15 recently vegetated monitoring nodes. This does not demonstrate absence of nearby bare habitat: 27 of 40 recently vegetated monitoring nodes fall outside the mapped polygon union, so the public map and point-monitoring states are not spatially interchangeable at this scale. Preserve the frozen 100-m / 12-node / 3-per-bay criteria and move bare-control qualification to preregistered field/imagery reconnaissance rather than relaxing the GIS threshold.
decision: Do not use the GIS layer alone to certify the canopy counterfactual subset. The direct hydrodynamic primary prospective study remains allowed. Canopy-specific attribution requires a separate field-validated bare-control subset passing the unchanged counterfactual criteria.
claim_boundary: The GIS failure is a field-design constraint, not evidence against hydrodynamic self-facilitation.
Do not relax the 100-m threshold or 3-per-bay requirement after seeing the result.
A monitoring node recorded as vegetated but outside the mapped polygon is a map-state mismatch, not automatically a bare habitat point.
Mapped edge proximity does not replace field depth matching, substrate/context inspection, wake assessment or simultaneous paired velocity measurement.
No future biological response was used.
